#/components/schemas/Kibana_HTTP_APIs_al.description: Composed query: a shared base with appendable breach and recovery segments.

base.description: Base ES|QL query. Time filters are applied automatically via the lookback window.

breach.description: Breach detection configuration. Omit to treat every base row as a breach.

segment.description: A clause appended to the end of the rule's ES|QL query. Required in breach blocks.

recovery.description: Recovery query segment. Required when recovery_strategy is "query".

segment.description: Appendable ES|QL segment for recovery detection.

code.description: Stable error code you can branch on, for example `INVALID_SCHEDULE` or `RULE_ALREADY_EXISTS`.

details.description: Optional extra information about the error, for example field validation issues or the `rule_id` when that ID already exists.

error.description: A short human-readable summary of the error category (e.g., "Not Found", "Bad Request"). Subject to change without notice. Do not parse or rely on its content.

message.description: A readable explanation of the error. The wording can change without notice. Do not parse this field.

artifacts.description: Optional objects attached to the rule, such as a runbook or a dashboard. Each item has `id`, `type`, and `data`. The shape of `data` depends on `type`. For example, a `runbook` uses `content` and a `dashboard` uses `dashboard_id`. Known types are validated against that shape. Unknown types are stored when `id`, `type`, and `data` are present.

anyOf.description: Creates an alert for each matching group and tracks it until it recovers. Use this when you want to detect a problem and notify or automate a response.
Stores each match as a rule event you can query. Alerts are not created and notifications are not sent.

kind.description: Whether the rule creates alerts (`alert`) or only stores matching events (`signal`).

anyOf.description: Keeps the alert's last status when the rule finds no data.
Not accepted when creating or updating rules. Do not send this value.
Marks the alert `inactive` the first time the rule finds no data for the alert.
Ignores runs where the rule finds no data.

no_data_strategy.description: How the rule behaves when it finds no data for a group. If you omit this field or set it to `none`, those runs are ignored. If you set `last_known_status` or `recover`, a standalone query (`query.format: standalone`) must include `query.no_data`. A composed query (`query.format: composed`) uses `query.base` to detect whether data is present. The `emit` value is not accepted when creating or updating rules.

anyOf.description: Recovers an alert when the breach query no longer returns matches.
Recovers an alert when a separate recovery query matches. Requires `query.recovery`.
The rule never marks an alert as `recovered`, even after the breach query stops returning matches.

recovery_strategy.description: The condition that marks an alert recovered. If omitted or set to `none`, recovery is disabled: the alert stays `active` even after the breach query stops returning matches, and `state_transition.recovering_count` / `recovering_timeframe` are not allowed. Set to `no_breach` to recover when the breach query stops returning matches. Set to `query` only when you also provide `query.recovery`.

state_transition.description: Consecutive-match or time requirements before an alert becomes `active` or `inactive`. Applies only when `kind` is `alert`.

pending_count.description: Number of consecutive matches required before the alert becomes `active`.

pending_operator.description: The operator that combines `pending_count` and `pending_timeframe`. `AND` requires both. `OR` requires either.

pending_timeframe.description: Time window used with `pending_count`, for example `5m` or `15m`.

recovering_count.description: Number of consecutive recoveries required before the alert becomes `inactive`.

recovering_operator.description: The operator that combines `recovering_count` and `recovering_timeframe`. `AND` requires both. `OR` requires either.

recovering_timeframe.description: Time window used with `recovering_count`, for example `5m` or `15m`.

time_field.description: Document field used as the event time when applying the lookback window. Defaults to `@timestamp`.

fields.description: Fields to group alerts by, e.g. ["host.name", "service.name"]. Should match ES|QL GROUP BY fields.

per_page.description: The number of rules per page.

total.description: The total number of rules matching the query.

builder_type.description: Identifies the rule builder that authored this rule (e.g. "threshold"). Absent for rules authored directly in ES|QL.

name.description: Rule name (must be unique within the space).

artifacts.description: Optional objects attached to the rule, such as a runbook or a dashboard. Each item has `id`, `type`, and `data`. The shape of `data` depends on `type`.
